title: Student Survey Questionnaire
purpose: This survey collects feedback for the Self-Assessment Report of the Mass Communication and Journalism Discipline. Your responses help improve teaching, facilities, and graduate outcomes.
confidentiality: This survey is strictly anonymous. Data will be aggregated for quality assurance purposes only. No individual will be identified in the reporting.
scale: 1 = Strongly Disagree / Very Poor | 2 = Disagree / Poor | 3 = Neutral / Average | 4 = Agree / Good | 5 = Strongly Agree / Excellent

questions.text: The academic calendar is followed without unexpected delays.
Theory class sizes are appropriate for effective learning.
Practical/studio class sizes allow individual attention.
I feel safe on campus and know how to report harassment.
I am aware of the program's vision, mission, and objectives.
The curriculum provides contemporary knowledge of media and communication.
Coursework has improved my research skills.
The program develops oral and written communication skills.
The curriculum enhances my ability to analyze media problems.
The program emphasizes professional ethics.
General Education courses are relevant and useful.
Internship/practical training is well-structured and beneficial.
Teachers use interactive methods rather than only lecturing.
Teaching encourages critical analysis and application.
Course outlines with outcomes and rubrics are provided at the start of term.
I receive timely feedback on assignments and exams.
Assessment fairly measures what I have learned.
Studio, lab, and fieldwork facilities are adequate.
The discipline encourages co-curricular participation.
Academic and career counseling are available.
The library collection and databases are adequate.
Computer labs and internet are adequate for my work.
There is a fair mechanism to handle student grievances.
Faculty members are knowledgeable and up-to-date.
Faculty members are accessible outside class hours.
Guest practitioners are invited to connect theory and practice.
What are the three biggest strengths of this program?
What are the major weaknesses or areas for improvement?
Is the program preparing you well for media and communication careers? Why or why not?
Any suggestions regarding studio, lab, or internship training?
